about: The Easter Preface from the 1962 Roman Missal, with the seasonal wording used from Low Sunday through the vigil of the Ascension. The Easter Vigil and Easter Sunday through the following Saturday use separate night and day variants. It is proper to the Masses of the season. In other Masses during this period, it is used only when they have no proper Preface.

s01.translation: Truly it is right and just, fitting and salutary, to praise You, Lord, at all times, but more gloriously especially at this time, because Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed. For He Himself is the true Lamb who has taken away the sins of the world. He has destroyed our death by dying and restored life by rising again. And therefore with Angels and Archangels, with Thrones and Dominions, and with all the host of the heavenly army, we sing the hymn of Your glory, evermore saying:

alignments.gloss: Truly it is right and just
for Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed
has destroyed our death by dying
has restored life by rising again

w019.explanation: Omni tempore and in hoc potissimum both describe when God is praised. Hoc refers to the present time.

w039.explanation: Moriendo means “by dying” and explains how Christ destroyed our death.

w043.explanation: Resurgendo means “by rising again” and explains how Christ restored life.
